Hey everyone, just a simple question for today. As the 2016 election creeps closer every day what does the Libertarian Party need to do or focus on to do well in the 2016 election(not just for president but for House and Senate.)

I feel the Libertarian Party needs to get more big name candidates for the upcoming election to get media coverage. Another thing that needs to be done(but it is out of our hands) is the Presidential Debate Commission needs to open up and allow the Libertarian nominee to debate. That would vastly swing votes in our favor.

But what do you think would help the party out?
What Does the Libertarian Party Need To Do in 2016?
Not try to play the fence. State its opinions clearly and don't try to sugar coat things.

Support a Tax Allocation Form. It would be similar to the 401k form where you choose where your money is going, except it's for the People to tell the govt where they can spend our money. Eliminates lobbyists, reduces pork spending, encourages civic participation, strips our political process of the chains of corporate money, allows for our divided country to heal by eliminating the major complaint from all political points along the spectrum: "I don't want my tax money paying for _____!". The programs and services that will be provided by the government will be done so in direct proportion to the amount of support those programs and services have from the people.

I think that it starts on the ground. The big names and debates help, but word of mouth is the first step.

It's amazing to me how many people hold staunch loyalty to one of the "big" parties and have no idea why. Challenging their ideas (gently) of what their allegiance really means, and giving them a healthy dose of common sense is the best medicine. Speaking calmly and rationally about how your views differ or are the same, and what the end game (what happens when you play the tape through on that issue?), and keeping a cool head in this time of polarized politics is the most marketable way to attract potential voters.

It's not a one time thing, it's an ongoing process. Be outspoken, insightful, and willing to listen and discuss whenever someone around you begins a political or current events conversation. Don't allow the responses to make you angry - "You threw away your vote"/ "Where's your tinfoil hat?" / "NAP sounds lame" / "Wait, WTF you really think that could work?" etc. - It won't help.

Just state your case, clear and simple.

With the way things have been going, what sensible individual wouldn't be interested in the principles and the value that the LP has to offer?

Another thing that needs to be done(but it is out of our hands) is the Presidential Debate Commission needs to open up and allow the Libertarian nominee to debate.
